prompt: Match each distance from the code to a defect it catches.

pairs.right: validation that lets a bad value through

prompt: Why do boxoffice's handler tests need no database at all?

choices.text: `go test` starts a PostgreSQL in memory
choices.why: `go test` starts no database; section 07 needs a real server for that.

choices.text: `httptest` intercepts every SQL query and answers it from memory
choices.why: `httptest` deals in HTTP requests and responses, never SQL.

choices.text: Each handler gets `memStore` through `Store`
choices.why: Right. The interface written so PostgreSQL could replace memory lets memory replace PostgreSQL here.

choices.text: Handlers read the database only on start-up
choices.why: `getEvent` asks its store on every request.

prompt: Why does the lesson test `pgStore`'s concurrent sales against PostgreSQL and not against a fake?

choices.text: A fake runs too fast to show the contention between transactions
choices.why: Speed is not the point: the fake is simply not the code under question.

choices.text: Go forbids interfaces in the test files of `package main`
choices.why: Test files use interfaces like any other Go file.

choices.text: The fake is not the thing being trusted
choices.why: Right. Only the database shows whether lesson 8's `UPDATE` is safe under concurrency.

choices.text: Mutexes do not work inside `go test`
choices.why: They work the same; `memStore` holds one throughout.

prompt: `TestGetEvent` calls `getEvent` directly. Why does it call `req.SetPathValue("id", tt.id)`?
hint: Who fills it in on a real request?

choices.text: Without it the recorder discards the body
choices.why: The recorder keeps whatever the handler writes; the path value is about the request.

choices.text: No mux ran, so nothing set it
choices.why: Right. The `ServeMux` sets `{id}` when it matches `/events/{id}`, and a direct call skips the mux.

choices.text: `NewRequest` refuses a URL with a number in it
choices.why: `NewRequest` accepts `/events/1` without complaint.

choices.text: It makes the test run in parallel
choices.why: Parallelism comes from `t.Parallel`, which these tests do not call.

prompt: Why does every case of `TestBuyTickets` get its own `newMemStore()`?

choices.text: Results would depend on case order
choices.why: Right. The purchase of two seats changes the store.

choices.text: `newMemStore` is cheap and Go discourages reuse
choices.why: Cost is not the reason; independence between cases is.

choices.text: A store survives only one request
choices.why: `memStore` keeps its events for as long as the value exists.

choices.text: The race detector demands it
choices.why: These cases run one after another; there is no race to detect.

prompt: For a failing case, what does `TestBuyTickets` check beyond the status?

choices.text: That the response took under a millisecond
choices.why: No case measures time.

choices.text: That an `X-Request-ID` header is present on the recorder
choices.why: A lone handler never passes through `requestID`; section 04 checks that header.

choices.text: That the store holds no new ticket
choices.why: The test reads the response only, never the store.

choices.text: A problem document
choices.why: Right. The body decodes as a `problem` with a matching `status`, sent as `application/problem+json`.

prompt: `go test` replays a passing result as `(cached)` while its inputs stay the same; passing the flag ___ turns that off for one run, as CI always does.
`newTestServer` calls `t.Helper()`. What does that change?

choices.text: It closes the server when the test ends
choices.why: That is `t.Cleanup(srv.Close)`.

choices.text: It runs the helper in its own goroutine
choices.why: `t.Helper` starts nothing; it only marks the function.

choices.text: Failures name the caller's line
choices.why: Right. That is why the skips pointed at the tests, not inside `testDB`.

choices.text: It hides the helper's output
choices.why: Output is untouched; only the reported line changes.

prompt: Match each token `TestStaffRoutes` sends to the status it expects on `/admin/report`.
`TestTheLogHoldsNoToken` passes today. Why keep it?

choices.text: It speeds up the other tests by warming the logger
choices.why: It warms nothing; it asserts something about the log.

choices.text: Go's test runner fails a package that has no log test
choices.why: No such rule exists.

choices.text: For the day somebody logs the headers to help debugging
choices.why: Right. Today `logRequests` logs no headers; the test makes that a promise.

choices.text: It checks the token reaches the handler intact
choices.why: It checks the log, not the handler.

prompt: `TestMain` sends the default logger to `io.Discard`. Why do none of the router tests call `t.Parallel()`?
hint: The default logger is one value for the whole process.

choices.text: `httptest.NewServer` refuses to start twice
choices.why: Each call gets a port of its own.

choices.text: Two tests would read each other's log lines
choices.why: Right. Changing the default logger is changing a global.

choices.text: `TestMain` runs again for every parallel test
choices.why: `TestMain` runs once per package.

choices.text: Parallel tests skip `t.Cleanup`
choices.why: Cleanups run for parallel tests as well.

prompt: Why does `load` take `getenv func(string) string` instead of calling `os.Getenv`?

choices.text: `os.Getenv` is slower than a function value
choices.why: Speed is not the reason; testability is.

choices.text: `os.Getenv` is unavailable in `package main`
choices.why: `main` itself passes `os.Getenv` to `load`.

choices.text: It lets `load` read Windows variables
choices.why: The platform has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: Tests hand it a map and leave the process's environment alone
choices.why: Right. Nothing a test sets reaches the process.

prompt: With lesson 14's `load`, the door and the manager got the same token. What happened at start-up?
hint: Two maps, one of them only for walking.

choices.text: A coin toss: map order picked the role
choices.why: Right. Go visits a map in a different order on purpose, so the role was a coin toss.

choices.text: `load` refused to start, with a clear message about it
choices.why: It accepted it: the test failed with `error <nil>`.

choices.text: The door was always the manager
choices.why: Not always: it depended on the order of that start.

choices.text: The server crashed on the first staff request
choices.why: Nothing crashed; one role silently replaced the other.

prompt: Order how the duplicate-token defect was handled in section 05.
items: write a case giving the door the manager's token
run it against lesson 14's `load` and watch it fail
read the roles from a slice and refuse a token that already has one

prompt: `TestLoadSecretFromFile` writes `from-a-file\n` into `t.TempDir()`. What is it checking?
hint: An editor leaves something at the end.

choices.text: That the file is deleted once it is read
choices.why: The framework deletes the directory; `load` deletes nothing.

choices.text: The trailing newline is trimmed
choices.why: Right. The token must be `from-a-file`, trimmed.

choices.text: That the file has mode 0600
choices.why: `load` never checks the mode.

choices.text: That a flag overrides the file
choices.why: Secrets have no flag.

prompt: Without `-race`, `TestConcurrentPurchases` printed `ok`. What was wrong with it?

choices.text: `memStore` sold more than ten seats
choices.why: The server sold exactly ten; its mutex held.

choices.text: `wg.Go` started fewer than fifty goroutines
choices.why: It started fifty; the race report is about `sold`.

choices.text: The event number 3 does not exist
choices.why: The test creates it; `newMemStore` already holds 1 and 2.

choices.text: Fifty goroutines ran `sold++` on one integer with nothing ordering them
choices.why: Right. Two goroutines both read 7 and both write 8, and the count comes out low now and then.

prompt: On which line of `concurrency_test.go` did the race detector report both accesses?
What is the fix for the race in `TestConcurrentPurchases`?

choices.text: Fewer buyers, so the goroutines rarely overlap
choices.why: Rarer is still a race; the detector would still find it.

choices.text: A mutex inside `memStore`
choices.why: `memStore` already holds one; the race is in the test's own counter.

choices.text: An `atomic.Int64`
choices.why: Right. `Add` is one indivisible step, and `Load` reads the total after `Wait`.

choices.text: Running the test without `-race`
choices.why: That hides the race; it does not remove it.

prompt: Which statement about the race detector matches section 06?

choices.text: It needs cgo and sees only races that run
choices.why: Right. That is why the test exists to make the concurrent case happen.

choices.text: It reads the source and finds every race in the package
choices.why: It watches execution; code that never runs concurrently shows nothing.

choices.text: It belongs in production binaries
choices.why: Section 08 keeps it to tests and staging runs because of its cost.

choices.text: It needs a PostgreSQL to compare against
choices.why: It needs a C compiler, not a database.

prompt: Why does `testDB` give every test a database with a random name?

choices.text: PostgreSQL forbids two tests in one database
choices.why: It forbids nothing of the kind; isolation is the test's choice.

choices.text: Random names make migrations faster
choices.why: The name has no effect on speed.

choices.text: To hide test data from `psql -l`
choices.why: The names start with `boxoffice_test_` and are dropped afterwards.

choices.text: Isolation between tests
choices.why: Right. Each starts from the migrations and the two seed events.

prompt: `testDB` registers the drop first and `pool.Close` second. In which order do they run?

choices.text: Drop, then close
choices.why: Cleanups run in reverse order of registration.

choices.text: Both at once, in two goroutines
choices.why: Cleanups run one after another.

choices.text: Close, then drop
choices.why: Right. The pool closes first, and `WITH (FORCE)` covers any connection still open.

choices.text: Only the drop; the pool leaks
choices.why: `t.Cleanup(pool.Close)` runs too.

prompt: Why does `TestASaleReachesTheHub` poll `pg_stat_activity` before selling?

choices.text: To count how many seats are left
choices.why: The seat count comes from the notification, 117.

choices.text: A sale before `listen` has run `LISTEN` is never heard
choices.why: Right. Waiting for the fact replaces a sleep that fails on a slow machine.

choices.text: PostgreSQL drops notifications for idle sessions
choices.why: An idle session that ran `LISTEN` receives them.

choices.text: To make the test slower and so more realistic
choices.why: The wait ends the moment `LISTEN` shows up.

prompt: Without `BOXOFFICE_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, what did the last line of the run say?

choices.text: `FAIL`
choices.why: Skipping is not failing; that is the danger.

choices.text: `SKIP` for the package
choices.why: The package line said `ok`.

choices.text: `[no test files]`
choices.why: That is for packages without tests.

choices.text: `ok`
choices.why: Right. Without `-v`, nothing says two tests did not run, so CI must set the variable.

prompt: The second identical run printed `(cached)`. Why is that a trap for a database test?
hint: What goes into the cache key?

choices.text: A cached run deletes the test databases
choices.why: A cached run runs nothing at all.

choices.text: The cache key covers the code, the flags and the variables read, and never the database's contents
choices.why: Right. `-count=1` turns the cache off, and CI always passes it.

choices.text: Cached results expire after a second
choices.why: They stay until an input changes.

choices.text: `(cached)` means the test failed earlier
choices.why: Only passing results are cached.

prompt: What coverage did `go test -count=1 -cover .` report for boxoffice?
How does the lesson read the coverage number?

choices.text: As a target to raise before every release
choices.why: Raising it by testing lines asserts nothing anybody needed.

choices.text: As proof that 60.6% of the code is correct
choices.why: A line that ran was not necessarily checked.

choices.text: As the share of tests that passed
choices.why: It counts statements, not tests.

choices.text: As a list of what no test has touched
choices.why: Right. `go tool cover -html` shows that list.

prompt: What did the race detector cost on boxoffice's whole suite?

choices.text: About double, still two seconds
choices.why: Right. For a suite this size the price is nothing.

choices.text: Ten times the time
choices.why: The runs took about 0.9 and 2.1 seconds.

choices.text: Nothing measurable on a suite this size
choices.why: The time roughly doubled.

choices.text: It failed to finish without a database
choices.why: The variable was set and both runs finished `ok`.

prompt: Match each moment to what section 08 runs then.

pairs.right: `go test -run` for the part you are changing
`go test -race -count=1 ./...` with the database variable set

prompt: Which statements match this lesson? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A test's own code runs concurrently too and follows the same rules
choices.why: Right. The race in section 06 was in the test.

choices.text: `t.Cleanup` runs only when the test passes
choices.why: It runs however the test ends.

choices.text: A skipped integration test prints `ok` without `-v`
choices.why: Right. That is why CI sets the variable.

choices.text: `httptest.NewServer` listens on a real port on `127.0.0.1`
choices.why: Right. The whole router is served over a real connection.

choices.text: Section 07's tests share one database to save time
choices.why: Each gets its own, created and dropped.

prompt: A colleague adds `t.Parallel()` to `TestTheLogHoldsNoToken` and `TestStaffRoutes`. What does the lesson predict?

choices.text: Nothing changes, since each has its own server
choices.why: The servers are separate; the default logger is not.

choices.text: The log test reads lines from the other test's requests
choices.why: Right. The default logger is one value for the process.

choices.text: `go test` refuses to compile them
choices.why: Both compile; the problem shows at run time.

choices.text: `TestMain` stops discarding the log
choices.why: `TestMain` ran once already; parallelism does not undo it.
